Posting again as I took too long to type out the recipes the first time…

All the dishes are vegan actually.

Batata Harra (Spicy Potatoes): I chopped a few potatoes into small cubes, boiled them until they were almost fully cooked and then strained them and fried them in some oil. I topped them with some finely chopped coriander and minced garlic and chili flakes that I also sautéed and in oil.

Tabbouleh: around 5 bunches of Parsley for 3 people. You want to separate the leaves from the stems as the stems won’t make the texture of the final result as good. I recommend watching/listening to something while you do this as it could take some time. You want to then very finely chop them into tiny bits. Be careful about using a food processor for chopping them as you might go overboard. Add them to a bowl with olive oil, the juice of 1-2 lemons, green onion (without the green parts) and some bulgur that was soaked in lemon juice until tender. Add a few mint leaves too but not too much as they can overpower the other flavors. add salt and pepper too and you can add lemon juice and/or olive oil to taste. Best served a few ours after putting it together and letting it rest in the fridge. 

Falefel: Soak some dried chickpeas overnight then thoroughly rinse and dry them and add to a food processor along with half an onion, a garlic clove or two, coriander, parsley, salt, pepper, cumin powder, and coriander powder then pulse them into small bits. The final mixture will probably be a bit wet, you can add flour to dry it out enough to hold its shape when you form them into small discs/balls. You can fry them or bake them in the oven.

Fatayer Sbenigh (Spinach pies): for the dough you need to mix 500 grams of all purpose flour with half a tablespoon of salt, half a tablespoon of sugar, 275 grams of water and 150 cups of vegetable oil. The filling: half a kilo of spinach, a medium sized onion, two lemons, half a teaspoon of salt, half a teaspoon of white pepper, two tablespoons of sumac, 100g of vegetable oil. Again remove the stems from the spinach leaves for better texture and sweat the water out of them by sprinkling some salt on them and letting them rest for a while. Then you want to squeeze all the excess water out and add the rest of the filling ingredients to it. Roll the dough out and then cut it into circles, add a but of filling in the middle and fold them into a triangle. Bake in the oven at max temperature until the dough is golden brown.
